customTheme.sampleNoteContent:
# Project Brainstorm

## Mobile App Features
- **Dark mode toggle** with smooth transitions
- **Offline support** for critical features
- **Push notifications** for reminders

## Backend Improvements
- **API rate limiting** to prevent abuse
- **Database optimization** for faster queries
- **Caching layer** for improved performance

*This is just a preview of the note content...*

migration.adminAccessDescription: This migration needs an admin. Ask one to run it.
migration.sharingDataMigrationDescription: Jotty needs to migrate your sharing data. It only runs once and needs an admin.
migration.noMigrationNeeded: Nothing to migrate, your data is already up to date.
migration.sharingNowWithData: Your sharing data now lives with your notes and folders.
migration.sharingMovesDescription: Sharing moves out of a central file and into your data. Folders can now be shared, and shared folders show up in your own sidebar instead of a separate section.
migration.whatsHappeningBody: Every share in .sharing.json is written into the frontmatter of the item it belongs to, and every folder gets a .category-info.json holding its identity, sharing and ordering. The old files are removed once the data has moved.
migration.sharingTravelsBody: Each shared item records who it is shared with in its own frontmatter, so moving or renaming it never breaks a share.
migration.folderSharingBody: Share a folder and everything inside it, now and in the future, is shared too. Recipients see it as a normal folder in their own sidebar.
migration.oneFilePerFolderBody: .order.json merges into .category-info.json, and ordering is keyed by uuid instead of filename.
migration.permissionsUnchangedBody: Read, edit and delete carry over exactly as they are today, per user and per item.
migration.backupWarningBody: This migration rewrites frontmatter across your notes and checklists and deletes the legacy .sharing.json and .order.json files. Back up your data folder before you continue.
migration.backupConfirmLabel: I've backed up my data folder.
migration.backupConfirmHint: Confirm you have a backup before you continue.
migration.sharingDataMigrated: Your sharing and ordering data is migrated.
migration.leftoversBody: The migration could not translate everything, so the legacy files below were left on disk untouched. You can fix the cause and run the migration again, or continue into the app now and deal with it later.
migration.overrideConfirmLabel: Continue anyway and stop showing this page.
migration.overrideConfirmHint: The leftover files stay on disk, but the app will treat your data as migrated. Any sharing or ordering listed above will not be applied until you migrate again, which you can do at any time from /migration?force=1.

attachments.title: Attachments update required
attachments.description: Attachments move next to the item they belong to, so whoever can read a note or board can see its images and files, and nobody else.
attachments.doneBody: Attachments now follow the sharing of the item they belong to.
attachments.adminOnly: An admin needs to move attachments next to the items they belong to before Jotty can be used again.
attachments.whatsHappeningBody: Every image, video and file a note or checklist embeds is linked into data/attachments, in a folder named after the item's uuid, and the item's URLs are rewritten to point there. Your original uploads stay where they are.
attachments.followsItemBody: Anyone who can read an item can open its attachments. Public items have public attachments, so the SERVE_PUBLIC_* variables are no longer needed.
attachments.noCopiesBody: Files are hardlinked, so the same image in ten notes still takes the space of one. If the disk can't hardlink they're copied.
attachments.encryptedTitle: Encrypted notes move on their next save
attachments.encryptedBody: Jotty can't read them, so their attachments move the next time the owner opens and saves them. Until then only the owner and admins can see those images.
attachments.backupBody: This migration rewrites URLs inside your notes and checklists. Back up your data folder before you continue. Every rewritten item is recorded in data/.migrations/attachments-v3.jsonl.
attachments.leftAlone: {count, plural, one {# thing was left alone, see below.} other {# things were left alone, see below.}}
attachments.copyMode: This disk can't hardlink, so {size} will be copied. {free} is free.
attachments.crossOwnerHint: These files were uploaded by someone who can edit the item, so they were moved in with it.

encrypted.title: Encrypted items
encrypted.hint: Their bodies can't be read without the passphrase, so their URLs stay as they are. Each one moves its own attachments the next time its owner opens and saves it.

locked.title: Items without a stored uuid
locked.hint: These need their frontmatter fixed before they can own attachments.

readOnly.title: Read-only folders
readOnly.hint: Jotty can't write to these folders, so nothing in them was changed.

clash.title: Duplicate uuids
clash.hint: Two files claim the same uuid. Repair the duplicate in Admin first, then run this again with ?force=1.

missing.title: Missing files
missing.hint: The URL points at a file that isn't on disk any more. The URL was left alone.

notFile.title: Not a regular file
notFile.hint: The URL points at a folder or a symlink, which are never moved.

crossOwner.title: Another user's files
crossOwner.hint: The file belongs to a user who can't edit this item, so it wasn't adopted. Its owner and admins can still open it.

foreign.title: URLs on another address
foreign.hint: Absolute URLs whose address isn't this instance's APP_URL were left alone.

loose.title: URLs in plain text
loose.hint: These sit in text rather than in a link or image, so they were left alone.

changing.title: Items still changing
changing.hint: These kept being edited while the migration ran. Run it again with ?force=1 to pick them up.

avatarMissing.title: Avatars that couldn't be found

lockedItem.title: Read-only until Jotty can add its id

reasons.empty: The file is empty, so Jotty hasn't written its id into it yet.
reasons.unparsable: Its frontmatter isn't valid YAML, so Jotty can't add its id without rewriting it.
reasons.foreignUuid: Its frontmatter already has a uuid that isn't a Jotty id, and Jotty won't overwrite it.

lockedItem.askEditor: Someone who can edit this item can fix it.
lockedItem.confirmMessage: Jotty will rewrite the frontmatter at the top of this file. It quotes values that aren't valid YAML, swaps tabs for spaces, moves a uuid that isn't a Jotty id to previousUuid, and adds its own uuid. The rest of the file stays as it is. Jotty can't undo this, so keep a copy if another app reads this frontmatter. You need edit access to this item, and its folder must be writable.
lockedItem.fixed: Fixed. You can edit this item now.
